history.text: I will take the message. I will not accuse anyone. It is a simple thing to deliver.

history.speaker: visitor
history.text: It was one of my own, Father. I used it for perhaps three weeks, buying grain for my own household and a few neighbors. I recall old Man Hemlock and Widow Elara being shortchanged.

history.speaker: priest
history.text: Then the first duty is plain: use that measure no more, and bring it to me when you return from Albert. How much grain do you judge Man Hemlock and Widow Elara each lost, and what did Albert say or threaten that persuaded you to do this?

history.speaker: visitor
history.text: Hemlock was shorted a good measure, perhaps a quarter of a sack. Elara, a bit less, maybe a tenth. He didn't threaten, Father, but spoke of needing to keep prices down, and that a little flexibility helped everyone.

history.speaker: priest
history.text: Calling theft flexibility does not make it charity. Restore a quarter-sack to Man Hemlock and a tenth to Widow Elara from what you bought, saying only that your reckoning was wrong. history.speaker: visitor
history.text: I will do as you ask, Father. I will make amends to Hemlock and Elara directly.

history.speaker: priest
history.text: That is a worthy beginning of repentance, Baldth. Think carefully before you return: were there any other buyers whom you may have shorted, even if you cannot recall the exact amount? Name them if you can, for amends must reach beyond the two we remember most clearly.

history.text: I will consider that, Father. I will think hard on anyone else I may have wronged.
